newsitem.title: KENYA: Zaire rebels attack Kisangani, airport threatened.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels attack Kisangani, airport threatened.

text.p: Zairean rebels have overrun main government defences on the eastern side of Kisangani in heavy fighting and the international airport is within firing range, a regional military source said on Saturday.

The source, who closely monitors the war between Laurent Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL) and Zaire's ragged army, said Zairean troops were looting as they fled the country's third largest city.
He said frightened civilians from Kisangani's 500,000-strong population were massing near the Zaire river hoping to board barges.
The main government defences on the east of Kisangani were taken in heavy pre-dawn fighting after the ADFL's two main frontline columns converged, he added.

"The rebels have overrun and captured the main government defence positions on the eastern side of Kisangani. Two main rebel columns have now merged outside the city and the airport is within firing range," the source said.
"The soldiers are looting Kisangani as they flee. Many are leaving by boats. There is confusion among the citizens," the source added.

The source said it appeared the rebels were ready to storm Kisangani airport, nerve centre of the government's proclaimed counter-offensive and main base for Serb mercenaries and Rwandan Hutu soldiers.
"They should have no problem taking the airport. We have detected movements that suggest they are readying to storm the airport," he added.
The source spoke after U.N. relief agencies and foreign embassies in Kinshasa said they were seeking ways to evacuate expatriates from Kisangani after reports of mortar fire outside the city.
"There has been fighting going on for five hours," a senior U.N. official in Kinshasa said late on Friday.
"We are looking for ways to evacuate our personnel and the French authorities are also searching for ways to help," the official said.

Aid workers in Kinshasa who were in contact with the city said the fighting began with mortar fire near the international airport on the outskirts of the town, where Zairean troops and their foreign mercenaries are concentrated.
Diplomats reported shooting inside Kisangani itself, but it was unclear if Zairean soldiers were fighting among themselves, looting or clashing with rebels.
A defence ministry spokesman in Kinshasa said reports the city was under rebel attack were false but conceded there may have been some shooting.
The battle for Kisangani, centre of Zairean military operations in the east of the vast central African country, has become pivotal with both rebels and government forces concentrating troops.

The fall of Kisangani, which the rebels claim is imminent though government forces deny this, would be the biggest setback for the government of ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko in a five-month rebel campaign. Rebels have already taken a vast area in the east of Zaire.
Kabila had given Zairean generals until Thursday to lay down weapons or face an all-out offensive on the strategic port at the head of the navigable section of the vast Zaire river.
